items.headline: Maple Leafs acquire Aatu Räty, send Jacob Quillan, Brandon Buhr to Canucks
items.description: The Maple Leafs acquired Aatu Räty, sending Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr to Vancouver.
items.take:
Per ESPN, the Maple Leafs acquired Aatu Räty from the Canucks, sending Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr to Vancouver.

Räty has not had much room to show anything so far this season. In four games he has one goal on 0.96 expected goals, so his results sit right at his chance quality, and he averages just 10.16 minutes a night. The more telling number is his 28.1 percent share of expected goals at 5-on-5, and Vancouver's share of expected goals was 14.1 percentage points better with him off the ice. Last season he had 4 goals and 14 points in 66 games, so this looks like a fourth-line depth piece, not a scoring upgrade, and his model rate of 0.75 expected goals per 60 backs that up.

Toronto's problem is not a hole at forward. The Leafs are 3-3-1 with a 44.4 percent share of expected goals overall and 43 percent at 5-on-5, while goalies have saved 5.0 goals above expected. That is a team getting more from its goaltending than its play deserves, and Räty's profile does little to change the territorial picture. For fantasy, he has no real value in this role.

items.headline: Senators' William Eklund set to miss 10-12 weeks after ankle surgery
items.description: Senators forward William Eklund is expected to be out 10 to 12 weeks after undergoing surgery to repair a torn tendon in his ankle suffered last week against the Flyers.
items.take:
Per ESPN, Senators forward William Eklund is expected to miss 10 to 12 weeks after surgery to repair a torn tendon in his ankle, an injury he suffered last week against the Flyers.

The timing hurts because Eklund had been driving play in a small sample. Through four games so far this season, Ottawa controlled 68.75 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, and the team's share of expected goals was 28.54 points better with him than without him. His own expected goals total of 2.66 against just one goal (a gap of 1.66) says the finishing had not caught up with the chances, so the points were likely to come. That is a real loss for fantasy owners, who were buying a player whose process outran his results. It also matters for the Senators, who sit at 5-2-0 but own just 48.8 percent of expected goals overall and 46 percent at five-on-five. Their record has leaned on goaltending (1.9 goals saved above expected). Losing one of the few forwards tilting the ice their way makes that cushion harder to count on.

items.headline: Which player has the most career points in NHL history?
items.description: Wayne Gretzky leads the list of NHL players with the most career points. Check out other top performers now.
items.take:
Per ESPN, Wayne Gretzky leads the list of NHL players with the most career points, and the piece looks at other top performers.

Two of the names still chasing that company are Alex Ovechkin and Sidney Crosby, and so far this season neither is giving much to build on. Ovechkin has 1 goal and 3 points in 7 games for WSH, on 1.24 expected goals, so he is just 0.24 goals short of what his chances warranted. The bigger issue is workload and context: he plays 13.94 minutes a game, and WSH controls only 35.48 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals with him out there. Crosby is at 2 goals and 4 points in 7 games for PIT, 0.48 below his 2.48 expected goals. He plays 19.76 minutes, and PIT has 47.76 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals in those shifts. Both teams also do better with each of them off the ice, by 17.37 points for WSH and 10.68 for PIT. The samples are small, but for fantasy owners the takeaway is that Crosby's minutes and chance volume support a rebound, while Ovechkin's shrinking role makes last season's 32 goals a harder mark to reach.

items.headline: Ducks rookie dons No. 95, channels Lightning McQueen in NHL debut
items.description: After a draft night trip to Disneyland to meet Lightning McQueen, the "Cars" synergy came full circle for the Ducks rookie's NHL debut.
items.take:
Per ESPN, Ducks rookie Roger McQueen wore No. 95 and channeled Lightning McQueen in his NHL debut, a "Cars" tie-in that came full circle after a draft night trip to Disneyland to meet the character.

The on-ice numbers are a one-game sample, so treat them lightly. McQueen played 11.43 minutes without a point, and his own expected goals were 0.13, so he finished 0.13 below expected. Anaheim controlled only 32.95 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals with him out there, and the team's share was 14.88 points better without him. That is a quiet, sheltered debut, nothing more. For fantasy purposes, he has no value yet at this usage. The more useful read is on Anaheim. The Ducks sit at 4-2-0, but their expected goals share is 48.6 percent (46 percent at 5-on-5), so they have been slightly outplayed. Two things are carrying them: they are 1.3 goals above expected, and their goaltending has saved 2.8 goals above expected so far this season. Both can fade, which is why the record looks better than the underlying play.

items.headline: Taylor Hall exits Hurricanes' 4-2 win with upper-body injury
items.description: Carolina Hurricanes veteran forward Taylor Hall, 34, who has three goals and five points this season, suffered an upper-body injury Tuesday night and did not return to his team's 4-2 victory over the Washington Capitals at Lenovo Center.
items.take:
Per ESPN, Carolina Hurricanes forward Taylor Hall, 34, suffered an upper-body injury Tuesday night and did not return to the team's 4-2 win over the Washington Capitals at Lenovo Center. Hall has three goals and five points this season.

The early numbers say the Hurricanes can absorb this better than the headline suggests, but Hall is not nothing. Across eight games so far this season, he has 3 goals against 2.22 expected goals from his own chances, a modest overperformance of 0.78 that doesn't point to a fluke. At 13.02 minutes a game he is a depth piece, yet Carolina controlled 63.48 percent of the 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share of points is 6.95 points better with him in the lineup. Carolina sits at 6-1-1 with a 61.8 percent expected goals share, so the foundation is sturdy. Still, last season's 18 goals and 48 points in 80 games show real secondary scoring that someone must replace. Fantasy managers should watch for a status update before dropping him, since his role is small but productive.
